title: Meridian workspace compatibility qualification register
description: Container for the final, product-neutral qualification (record_type: workspace-compatibility-qualification) of one workspace/repository's run through the meridian-workspace-compatibility program: discovery and rule intake (existing-project-compatibility-mode.schema.json, composing instruction-source-registry.schema.json and controlled-rule-intake.schema.json), an optional migration plan (instance-data-migration.schema.json) and an optional canonical export (instance-canonical-export.schema.json). Each entry is a scoped record: its envelope (identity, scope, origin, authority) is validated against the same scoped-record.schema.json every other operating-model contract composes with, and this schema is not a second envelope schema. The record does NOT embed any of the three composed records: payload.workspace_connection_ref/migration_plan_ref/canonical_export_ref are CLOSED pinned references, resolved through an external boundary at the library level and checked there against the REAL evaluateExistingProjectCompatibilityMode/evaluateInstanceDataMigration/evaluateInstanceCanonicalExport — never a second, competing shape for any of the three, and never a raw imported field (raw_excerpt, normalized_text, or any secret-bearing value) persisted in this record. All three references pin an exact sha256 content digest of the resolved record — computeConnectionDigest for the workspace connection scan, computePlanFingerprint/computeExportDigest for the migration plan and canonical export — never a bare id/reference an independent resolver could satisfy with different content under the same label. payload.qualification_state is a closed, RECOMPUTED verdict — QUALIFIED, BLOCKED or UNVERIFIED — checked at the library level against the composed evaluations' own outcome (including whether any resolved rule candidate is still an undecided applicability_state candidate, which alone forces UNVERIFIED and never QUALIFIED); a declared state that does not match the recomputed one is rejected, never trusted on its own. blockers/open_questions are closed to qualification_state: blockers is non-empty exactly when BLOCKED, open_questions is non-empty exactly when UNVERIFIED. This package does not migrate, export, scan, or accept any rule; it only qualifies — declares one closed verdict over records produced by the five packages it composes. The contract is a mandatory part of the Kernel: an absent schema or absent fixtures is a validator FAIL, not an informational skip. The normative document is standards/workspace/workspace-compatibility-qualification.md.

pinned_ref.description: A closed reference resolved through an external boundary — never an embedded body. sha256 is mandatory on all three uses of this shape in this schema: the exact composed version's own recomputed content digest (computeConnectionDigest/computePlanFingerprint/computeExportDigest), never a bare id/reference an independent resolver could satisfy with different content under the same label.

workspace_connection_ref.description: Always required: a qualification without a pinned, resolvable workspace connection scan does not exist. sha256 pins the resolved record's own recomputed computeConnectionDigest.

migration_plan_ref.description: null when this qualification composes no migration plan; otherwise a pinned reference to one FULL instance-data-migration entry, sha256-pinned to its recomputed plan_fingerprint.

canonical_export_ref.description: null when no canonical export is composed; otherwise a pinned reference to one FULL instance-canonical-export entry, sha256-pinned to its recomputed digest. Present only meaningfully alongside a non-null migration_plan_ref.
